lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0005-format-interop/README.md stage 11 (Attention/engine strategy): "11. Attention/engine strategy: the largest blocked surface is not a format: upstream vLLM's V1 engine requires FlashAttention or FlashInfer (sm_80+) and the V0/xformers path Turing relied on has been removed, so current upstream has no working sm_75 engine at all. This fork retains the Turing-capable engine (CUDA-graph validated); the strategy row is keeping that engine healthy against upstream drift, plus a Triton-attention option (Triton runs on sm_75) as the portable fallback." The same file's sequencing note marks this the load-bearing row: "The engine row (11) is the load-bearing one: without a Turing engine, every other row is unreachable on current upstream." Fork state per MEMORY.md 2026-08-27: slartibardfast/vllm is the hosted fork synced to upstream (the pin is an ancestor), branch sm75-marlin; graph-capture replay validation recorded in turing_lab/probes/cuda_graph_validation.md. Host rigs: 2x Quadro RTX 6000 (TU102, sm_75, 24 GB), clocks locked 1455 MHz.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the sm75 floor in serving engines is not one line but a bifurcated, actively drifting surface; every claim in the plan/0005 stage-11 row checks out against upstream records, with one correction on which PR caused the v0.24.0 drop. (1) vLLM main is at the v0.28.0 era (v0.28.0 released 2026-08-26; v0.26.0 2026-07-27) and STILL floors FlashInfer at SM80: vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py supports_compute_capability returns >= DeviceCapability(8,0) with the comment "FlashInfer supports SM75+, but is currently broken on SM75 (Turing)" citing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3620 and fix PR #3621, "Temporarily raise the floor to SM80 so it is not auto-selected on SM75 until that fix lands... Revert to DeviceCapability(7, 5) once it lands". (2) The floor raise landed via commit cf16db7 inside vLLM PR #45375 ("[Quant] Enable modelopt_mixed on Turing (SM75)", merged 2026-06-23), i.e. it was a deliberate, temporary floor raise paired with extending modelopt_mixed to sm75 via Marlin W4A16/MarlinFP8 - NOT the accidental side effect of the #46492 flashinfer_cutlass refactor that issue #47549's reporter suspected (both are in v0.24.0). (3) Restore path is real but stalled: flashinfer PR #3526 ("keep HEAD_DIM 256 prefill within 64 KiB smem on SM75/SM70", fixes #3528; 65584->65536 B via empty-base-optimization mixins) merged 2026-07-22; the head_dim-128 prefill invalid-argument bug flashinfer#3620 (T4, flashinfer 0.6.12, CUDA 13, P1, assigned) is still open with fix PR #3621 open; vLLM draft PR #46943 by rbray89 (opened 2026-06-28, still draft, no milestone) reverts the floor to 7.5 and a commenter notes it "will be relevant when vllm adopts the incoming version of flashinfer" (vLLM main is on the FlashInfer 0.6.x line, 0.6.18 per current docs). (4) Issue #47549 ("REGRESSION: FP8 KV cache FlashInfer no longer available as attention backend on SM75 in v0.24.0", opened 2026-07-03 by ptempier, STILL OPEN, zero maintainer response) is the fleet evidence: 18x Quadro RTX 8000 impacted; v0.23.0 offered candidates ['FLASHINFER','TRITON_ATTN'], v0.24.0 offers only ['TRITON_ATTN']; since Triton attn rejects fp8 KV on cc 7.5, --kv-cache-dtype fp8 now ValueErrors at startup; measured: KV capacity halved 287,744 -> ~143,000 tokens (fp16 fallback) and decode at ~22K ctx collapsed from ~5-11 tok/s to ~0.8-1.1 tok/s; reporter pins vllm-openai:v0.23.0 as the workaround. (5) The other floors hold: TensorRT-LLM officially requires compute capability 8.0+ (Ampere) - overview/installation docs; SGLang is effectively Ampere+ (#7467 closed inactive after the Triton 3.3 f16-conversion crash on T4, workaround triton==3.2.0; team signaled dropping sm75 in v0.5 per #6006; #1058 "T4 not work"; Clarifai docs state "Ampere or newer, compute capability >= 8.0"). (6) Model-level gates on sm75 remain: Qwen3-VL request #29743 (opened 2025-11-30, closed NOT PLANNED as stale at 90 days) - model code accepts only FLASH_ATTN/TORCH_SDPA/ROCM_AITER_FA, none viable on sm75, --enforce-eager "extremely slow (less than 10 tokens/s)" at ~20% throughput; Gemma4 #38918 (opened 2026-04-03, open, no triage) - ALL backends blocked on 2x RTX 2080 Ti under v0.19.1rc1.dev4: FLASH_ATTN auto-excluded (SM>=8.0), FLASHINFER rejects head_size 512 (supports 64/128/256), TRITON_ATTN and FLEX_ATTENTION both die on Triton OutOfResources "Required: 98304, Hardware limit: 65536" (96 KB shared memory vs Turing's 64 KB/SM ceiling) for head_dim 256 sliding / 512 global. (7) The one sm75-positive upstream lane is quantization: official docs table marks "Marlin (GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/FP4)" supported from Turing onward (footnote "Turing does not support Marlin MXFP4"), AWQ from Turing, GPTQ from Volta, and modelopt_mixed since #45375.
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing-class hardware (T4/2080 Ti/RTX 6000/RTX 8000) today, per upstream records: the engine runs, but only on the TRITON_ATTN leg, at roughly half the KV capacity and 5-10x slower long-context decode than the FlashInfer leg that v0.23.0 still had. Attention-backend candidate matrix for sm75 (dated; vLLM V1, CUDA platform): (a) FLASH_ATTN (FA2) - NOT viable: FlashAttentionBackend.supports_compute_capability >= DeviceCapability(8,0) (verified in v0.11.1 source and unchanged in current docs "FA2 >= 8.0"); upstream flash-attn itself targets Ampere+ (FA3 sm90, FA4 sm100+); Turing was never supported by FA2 wheels. (b) FLASHINFER - viable from v0.11.1 (floor (7,5), inclusive, through (12,1)) until v0.24.0 raised it to (8,0); on sm75 it was the auto-selected backend (priority FLASH_ATTN -> FLASHINFER -> TRITON_ATTN -> FLEX_ATTENTION, first valid wins, FA rejected at 8.0 check) and uniquely carried fp8 KV: supported_kv_cache_dtypes auto/fp8/fp8_e4m3/fp8_e5m2 (software conversion, no FP8 tensor cores needed), head sizes [64,128,256]; this is exactly the 2x-KV-capacity lever lost in v0.24.0 (#47549: 287,744 vs ~143,000 tokens on a 48 GB RTX 8000, and 5-11 -> 0.8-1.1 tok/s decode at 22K ctx when forced to fp16/Triton); restore is one capability-constant revert (draft PR #46943) once a FlashInfer release carries the sm75 prefill fixes (#3526 merged 2026-07-22 for head_dim 256; #3621 still open for head_dim 128); FlashInfer's own stated floor is "SM75 (Turing) and later". (c) TRITON_ATTN - the only auto-candidate on sm75 since v0.24.0 ("Any" compute capability in the official matrix); works for GQA-class models in fp16/fp32 KV; hard limits observed: fp8 KV raises "FP8 KV cache is not supported by the Triton attention backend" on cc 7.5 (#47549), and head_dim >128 risks the 64 KB shared-memory ceiling (#38918: 98304 B required vs 65536 for head_dim 256/512; TILE_SIZE reduction is the reporter's untested suggestion). (d) FLEX_ATTENTION - "Any" capability; was the V1 DEFAULT for sm70/sm75 in the v0.10.x-v0.11.0 era (v0.11.0 cuda.py: "FlexAttention is the default for older GPUs"); torch.compile/Inductor -> Triton codegen path, so it inherits the Triton sm75 codegen risks below and the same smem ceiling (#38918 fails during CUDA-graph warmup). (e) XFORMERS - the V0-era Turing workhorse; V1 backend file still existed at v0.11.1 but is defunct for the LLM path (per #29743 it does not provide the FA2-compatible context-layer behavior Qwen3-VL needs); V0 engine/executors were removed across the v0.11.x line (#27142 et al.); absent from the current backend registry entirely. (f) TORCH_SDPA - defunct for serving ("this tag is only used for ViT", #29743); current ViT path for sub-8.0 GPUs offers TORCH_SDPA as fallback. (g) TRT-LLM/trtllm-gen attention - not viable: trtllm-gen paths inside vLLM are SM100-family only, and TRT-LLM itself is Ampere+ (CC 8.0). (h) FlashMLA/MLA stack - FlashMLA sm90/sm100 only; TRITON_MLA is "Any" capability, i.e. the only DeepSeek-class option on Turing (plan/0005 stage 12, unmeasured on Turing). Measured quant-side numbers on sm75 (upstream, RTX 2080 Ti, PR #29901): Marlin-Turing vs torch-fp16 GPTQ 2-3.3x faster at batch 1 (0.0097 ms vs 0.0320 ms at n=4096,k=2048,m=1), w4a8-int8 consistently fastest, loses to GPTQ exllama v2 at large batch (exllama switches to dequant+cublas for m>8); MXFP4 impossible (needs BF16 activations), so NVFP4 arrives via Marlin W4A16 emulation and FP8 dense via MarlinFP8, none needing native FP8 tensor cores. Triton codegen path for sm75 (gates the TRITON_ATTN/FLEX fallbacks): pre-Ampere dots lower to the mma.m16n8k8 tensor-core path (m16n8k16 requires sm80 - the same constraint MEMORY.md 2026-08-27 recorded for the Marlin port, which emulates k16 as two stacked k8 issues) with FMA fallback for non-dot ops; the Triton 3.3.0/3.3.1 window (May-Jul 2025) crashed fp16 ops on cc<8.0 with "Unsupported conversion from f16 to f16" / "LLVM ERROR: Unsupported rounding mode for conversion" (triton#6698, RTX 2080 Ti, IR target cuda:75; root cause a botched f32->f16->f32 re-conversion in the fp8-conversion lowering, fixed by triton#7585 merged 2025-07-22, first carried by the 3.4 line [uncertain: exact release]); community practice is pinning triton<=3.2 (SGLang #7467: downgrading to 3.2.0 fixed the T4 crash), so the fork's portable-Triton-attention fallback must ride a known-good Triton pin (<=3.2 or a >=3.4 verified on sm75).

[2025-11-18, v0.11.1] THE RE-ENABLE: FlashInfer added as the default CUDA dependency (#26443); backend selection refactored to a priority list (FLASH_ATTN -> FLASHINFER -> TRITON_ATTN -> FLEX_ATTENTION on non-Blackwell); with FA gated at >=8.0 and FlashInfer at >=7.5, Turing auto-selects FlashInfer - community reports a massive speedup and FP16 serving working again on Turing/Volta (r/LocalLLaMA, Nov 2025; exact re-enable PR not identified in release notes, mechanism inferred [uncertain]); fp8 KV (e4m3/e5m2) available on sm75 from this line. [2025-12-16/19, merged] PR #29901 Marlin kernel port for Turing sm75 (no cp.async -> synchronous copies; no m16n8k16 -> two stacked m16n8k8; FP16 accumulator because FP32-acc halves MMA throughput on Turing; GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/NVFP4, INT8 act for GPTQ/AWQ; MXFP4 excluded); PR #31000 enables compressed-tensors Marlin on Turing (get_min_capability 8.0 -> 7.5; follow-up #31008); visible in v0.13.0rc2 nightlies. [2026-01-20, v0.14.0] release notes list "Marlin for Turing (sm75)" citing exactly #29901 and #31000; T4/T10/2080 Ti class can run 32B AWQ. [2026-06-12, flashinfer side] #3620 opened: BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache fails on T4 with CUDA invalid argument (shared-memory miscount vs the 64 KB opt-in cap; SM80+'s 164 KB masks it); same window flashinfer#3528/#3526 for head_dim 256. [2026-06-15, v0.23.0] LAST-GOOD FlashInfer-on-sm75 base: candidates ['FLASHINFER','TRITON_ATTN'], FlashInfer 0.6.12 (#44036); this is the pin the fork should treat as the last-good upstream base for the engine row. [2026-06-23, main] commit cf16db7 in PR #45375 raises FlashInfer floor (7,5)->(8,0), deliberately and temporarily, citing flashinfer#3620/#3621. [2026-06-29, v0.24.0] THE DROP ships: sm75 candidates reduced to ['TRITON_ATTN']; fp8 KV ValueErrors at startup on sm75; #47549 opened 2026-07-03 (open, no maintainer response) documents the 18x RTX 8000 fleet impact; same release also extends modelopt_mixed to sm75 (#45375) - the floor raise and the Turing quant enable rode in together. effort_value.effort_estimate: Small code delta plus a standing audit row - not a kernel campaign (plan/0002 owns the kernels). Concretely: (1) one-constant capability revert in the fork's vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py (7,5 floor, or adopt upstream PR #46943 verbatim once it lands) with a pinned sm75-capable FlashInfer (>= a release carrying #3526/#3621; today that means building/holding a wheel); (2) a candidate-list regression test: assert sm75 offers FLASHINFER + TRITON_ATTN and that fp8 KV is accepted, run per rebase (this is the test that would have caught v0.24.0 upstream); (3) a known-good Triton pin decision for the TRITON_ATTN/FLEX fallbacks (<=3.2 or verified >=3.4 on sm75) recorded in environment.md. Estimate: 1-2 sessions to land, then a per-upstream-release drift check folded into the rebase ritual.
effort_value.unlocks: Every other plan/0005 row (stages 1-10, 12-13): FP8-residency emulation, AutoRound W4/W2, NVFP4/MXFP4 adapters, BF16 recast, MLA emulation, and the operator's Qwen3-class ~27B both-card target all ride a Turing-capable engine. Directly, the FlashInfer leg restores: 2x KV capacity via fp8 e4m3 KV (287,744 vs ~143,000 tokens measured on a 48 GB card), 5-10x long-context decode (5-11 vs 0.8-1.1 tok/s at 22K ctx), CUDA-graph-covered FlashInfer decode, and the only current path toward Qwen3-VL-class multimodal once a context-layer backend exists (upstream closed #29743 not-planned, so it is fork-or-nothing). Also unblocks MTP/spec-decode paths that prefer FlashInfer metadata plumbing.
effort_value.dependency_order: First: this row - it gates all serving. Repo-internal: rides the plan/0003 harness (float64 oracle, ladder, gates) which already exists; independent of the plan/0002 Marlin kernel campaign (which it gates at the serving-integration step); plan/0004 TP shard work proceeds in parallel. External prerequisites: an sm75-capable FlashInfer artifact (upstream releases do not guarantee sm75 wheels - the #3620 reporter shipped a self-built SM75 wheelhouse; the fork needs its own pinned build or the v0.23.0-era 0.6.12 pin until #3526/#3621 land in a release), and the Triton pin decision. Parallel-safe: candidate-list test, drift ledger maintenance, v0.23.0-vs-main A/B probe.
effort_value.risk_notes: Upstream-drift exposure is the defining risk and is now proven twice (V0/xformers removal across v0.11.x; the v0.24.0 FlashInfer floor raise) - and the drift was SILENT: no error, just a shorter candidate list until fp8 KV happened to raise, so only an explicit candidate-assertion test catches the next one. Correctness/numerics: FlashInfer sm75 kernels live exactly at the 64 KB opt-in shared-memory ceiling - 48-96 B of alignment padding flips launch success (#3526's 65584->65536 fix), so sm75 breakage is config-dependent (head_dim, dtype) and can surface as a runtime cudaErrorInvalidValue rather than a load-time gate; the head_dim-128 prefill case (#3620) is still open upstream. Marlin-on-Turing ships with an FP16 accumulator (FP32-acc halves throughput on sm75), a genuine numerics downgrade vs other architectures' FP32 accumulation - accumulation-order and outlier sensitivity belongs in the oracle gates, and the fork's own m16n8k8 findings (MEMORY 2026-08-27) independently confirm the halved-FP32-rate constraint. Silent-fallback semantics: FlashInfer->TRITON_ATTN substitution changes numerics (different accumulation/split-K order) at fp16-visible scale - fine for statistical gates, wrong for bitwise expectations. Triton window: 3.3.x is a standing crash risk (not silent corruption - hard LLVM error) on the Flex/Triton fallbacks. bf16 absence on sm75 forces fp16 recast with overflow checks (>65504 outliers must be reported, never truncated - plan stage 10 contract).
effort_value.determinism_class: Statistical, not bitwise, by design: FlashInfer, TRITON_ATTN, and FLEX_ATTENTION implement attention with different tile shapes, accumulation orders, and split-K/decode strategies, so backend swaps move logits at fp16-roundoff scale even with identical inputs; within one backend, run-to-run variance sources are FlashInfer autotune caches (plan/kernel selection can differ across warmups and restarts) and CUDA-graph capture sets, while restart-to-restart adds autotune-cache persistence effects; Triton kernels add config-search nondeterminism (and the OutOfResources behavior on sm75 depends on tile selection). The float64-oracle + median-of-N gate discipline therefore must hold per-backend (oracle-check the kernel math - the FP8-recast reference is exact/lossless, so oracle-attestation is available - and gate throughput on medians), never across backends bitwise; kernel-selection-dependent outputs (autotune winners) should be pinned in transcripts so a rebase that silently re-autotunes is visible. Graph replay determinism for the fork's own kernels is already validated (turing_lab cuda_graph_validation), and the engine row inherits that: replay-stable decode is part of the acceptance, with attention-backend identity recorded in every serving transcript.

decision.priority_signal: FOR doing this next: it is the plan's own load-bearing row (every format/interop row is unreachable without it); the upstream window is demonstrably unstable - the drop shipped unannounced inside a Turing-friendly PR (#45375), the regression issue #47549 has sat open with zero maintainer response since 2026-07-03, the restore PR #46943 has sat in draft since 2026-06-28, and the FlashInfer head_dim-128 fix is still open - so waiting for upstream means riding a one-backend engine (TRITON_ATTN) with 2x KV-capacity and 5-10x long-ctx decode penalties measured on a real 18-GPU fleet; the fix in-fork is one capability constant plus a pinned sm75 FlashInfer build, the cheapest possible load-bearing win. AGAINST: upstream restoration looks likely within a few releases (#3526 already merged, #46943 ready), which would make the fork's patch a trivial rebase; and the plan's 'no working sm_75 engine at all' is now slightly overstated for GQA-class models - v0.24.0+ still serves them on TRITON_ATTN - the real gap being fp8-KV capacity, large-head-dim models (Gemma4), and multimodal (Qwen3-VL); so the item is a pin-and-assert maintenance row rather than an emergency. Net: do it now, cheaply, because the drift itself (not any single drop) is the liability and the assertion test is the only durable defense.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 probe, oracle-first, no timing until numerics proven, under a day on the existing TU102 host: (1) pin vLLM v0.23.0 (vllm-openai:v0.23.0 image or the fork's source at that tag) with its FlashInfer 0.6.12, GPU 0, a fixed 8B-class GPTQ checkpoint; run --attention-backend FLASHINFER with --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 and again with fp16; oracle-check outputs against the float64 reference of the checkpoint values (the E4M3 recast is lossless, so the reference is exact), median-of-N decode, and record the candidate list + measured KV token capacity - this settles the last-good-base claim empirically. (2) Same build with VLLM_USE_V1 attention selection on default, assert candidates == ['FLASHINFER','TRITON_ATTN']. (3) Apply the one-constant floor revert (7,5) to the fork's main-sync and re-run (1); if a post-0.6.12 FlashInfer with #3526 is built, exercise head_dim 128 AND 256 prefill to map the open-#3620 boundary. (4) Cross-check TRITON_ATTN on the same prompts for the statistical band. Deliverable: a dated ledger entry (v0.23.0 vs reverted-main, numerics transcripts, KV capacities, candidate lists) that both proves the fork's engine row and becomes the regression test's expected values.
